**PM correction — my dispatch instruction was wrong, and the dev was right to disobey it.** Recording this before CI converges, because it is a fact about the repo rather than a verdict on the PR.

## What I told it, and why it would have silently failed

My brief said: *"⛔ **Never hand-edit a generated file** to match; run the generator and commit what it produces."* That is the right default almost everywhere in this repo. It is **wrong for the i18n bundle**, and following it here would have produced a no-op that looked like success.

The dev measured why: **`check-i18n-bundles.mjs` runs in MERGE mode.** It preserves every already-committed value — English included — across regeneration, and reacts only to **added or dropped keys**, never to a **changed** string. So `--write` reports "in sync", touches nothing, and `en.objects.generated.ts` keeps the old uncited text **forever**, while the source-of-truth `description` says something different. A silent divergence between a field's declaration and its shipped help text — which is the same class of defect this card exists to close.

It hand-edited the one `client_secret.help` value to match verbatim, and cited AGENTS.md's own guardrail for it: *"editing a string is fine, only adding/dropping keys is drift."* ⇒ **My ⛔ was overridden by a rule that outranks it, and the dev checked before acting rather than after.** That is the behaviour I want; a dev that had obeyed me literally would have shipped the bug.

## ⇒ The generalisable fact, which is worth more than this card

⛔ **`.generated.ts` does not mean "fully generator-owned" in this repo.** The i18n bundles are **merge-maintained**: the generator owns the key *set*, humans own the *values*. So:

- **changing a string** ⇒ hand-edit the bundle value; the generator will not do it for you and will not tell you it did not;
- **adding or removing a key** ⇒ run the generator; that is the drift it detects.

The three translated locales (`es-ES` / `ja-JP` / `zh-CN`) are independently hand-maintained and were correctly left untouched.

## Two more things it got right without being told twice

- **The card's own citation had drifted.** `auth-manager.ts:2473` now falls inside the **phoneNumber** plugin block, not `oidcProvider`. It cited the **symbol** (`AuthManager.buildPluginList()`, oidcProvider branch) instead of a line number that will drift again — exactly the instruction, applied to the card rather than just to the code.
- **It re-verified the underlying claim** against the installed `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.0-rc.2` dist rather than trusting #8011: `storeClientSecret` has **no cleartext branch at all** — every path hashes, encrypts or throws — and the default resolves to `'hashed'` because neither `storeClientSecret` nor `disableJwtPlugin` is set anywhere in `packages/` while jwt is registered unconditionally alongside `oauthProvider`.

It also ran **all 43 `check:*` steps** from the `ESLint` job and named them, plus `check:i18n` — which `dispatch-gates.mjs` cannot derive, because it walks `packages/` dynamically rather than matching a path literal. And it reported honestly that `check:i18n-coverage` could **not** be measured locally (an unrelated `connector-mcp` build gap in a scoped worktree) rather than letting a skipped gate read as a passed one.

ACCEPT verdict follows once every gate job's own `conclusion` is in.

The substantive correction is recorded above (comment `5277872855`) and stands: **my "never hand-edit a generated file" instruction was wrong for this file**, and following it would have shipped a silent divergence. ⛔ Not re-litigated here.

## Why this accepts at `sonnet` tier without qualification

I dispatched this as a mechanical card and told it to **stop and report rather than improvise** if the task turned out not to be what that assumed. It did neither of the failure modes available to it:

- it **did not improvise** — when my ⛔ collided with a repo rule, it found AGENTS.md's own guardrail and cited it rather than inventing a justification;
- it **did not stop unnecessarily** — regenerating vs hand-editing was a mechanical question with a discoverable answer, so discovering it was the work, not an escalation.

That is the correct reading of a stop-condition: stop when the *decision* is not yours, not when the *task* is harder than billed.

Three more things it got right unprompted:

- **It re-verified the underlying claim** against the installed `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.0-rc.2` dist rather than trusting #8011's word: `storeClientSecret` has **no cleartext branch at all**, and the default resolves to `'hashed'` because neither `storeClientSecret` nor `disableJwtPlugin` is set anywhere in `packages/` while jwt is registered unconditionally alongside `oauthProvider`. The card asked for a citation; it checked the citation was true first.
- **It caught the card's own citation drifting.** `auth-manager.ts:2473` now falls inside the **phoneNumber** plugin block, not `oidcProvider` — so it cited the **symbol** (`AuthManager.buildPluginList()`, oidcProvider branch) instead of a line number that will drift again. ⇒ the whole point of this card was to stop a claim being re-measured a third time; a citation that rots would have guaranteed a fourth.
- **It named an un-measurable gate instead of letting it read as passed.** `check:i18n-coverage` could not run locally (an unrelated `connector-mcp` build gap in a scoped worktree). ⭐ **A named un-measured gate is worth more than a silent one** — that is the difference between a report and a claim.

It ran all 43 `check:*` steps from the `ESLint` job and named them, plus `check:i18n` — which `dispatch-gates.mjs` **cannot** derive, because it walks `packages/` dynamically rather than matching a path literal. That is now the third instance of that structural gap and it is recorded on the seat.

Marking ready and enqueuing; landing confirmed by a commit on `origin/main`.

So running the generator on a reworded description reports "in sync", touches nothing, and ships the stale text forever. **Changing a string requires a hand edit; adding or removing a key is what the generator owns.** Both are recorded on the seat post (#6367).
